correctness.rationale: The amended exact jump result and the comparison baseline both check. A nonempty white fort has no outside vertex with exactly one neighbor in it. Such a set cannot lose its first vertex to a force, and a stalled nonempty white set is itself a fort. Independently enumerated all 24204 nonempty forts, marked their supersets, and excluded precisely the seeds whose complements contain a fort. No seed below size seven forces; at seven there are 6912, split evenly by three versus four selected points. All unordered pairs of minima were tested for symmetric difference of size two, and slides additionally for base adjacency. The six explicitly checked incidence generators generate a group of size 216, inducing 29 orbits of size 216 and six of size 108. Full breadth-first distance layers from each orbit give a single connected 97524-edge jump graph with eccentricity seven at all 6912 states, and a connected 10962-edge slide baseline with counts 16:648,17:4968,18:1296. Since the group preserves both move rules, the orbit-weighted check is exhaustive for these invariants. The amended wording distinguishes host automorphisms from automorphisms of the state graphs.
residual_risks: Only the finite order-three incidence graph and the two stated minimum-preserving rules. Bundled code was inspected, not executed; the independent fort-based check is a separate reproduction.

value.rationale: On a canonical cubic girth-six incidence graph, the maximum optimal-seed travel requirement is a natural minimum-preserving mobility invariant. The amended theorem answers it from every starting seed, rather than just showing reachability (already implied by connected slides). Uniform jump eccentricity seven contrasts with variation and diameter eighteen for local moves on exactly the same seed family. This gives a concrete and reproducible finite benchmark for the established zero-forcing graph, with no reliance on claiming the covered state or slide census as new.
residual_risks: The contrast neither classifies other biaffine graphs nor implies general complexity, forcing-time or optimal-control claims.
